failure_name: Healthy EHI Mean Below Target (93.24 vs >=95.0)
key_timestamps: t in [0, 30] s (initial warm-up transient across all scenarios)
primary_root_cause: Static surrogate reference does not model dynamic thermal lag (tau=25s for CHT/EGT, tau=60s for oil temp). Engine starts at ambient+25C and takes 40-60s to reach equilibrium, producing large negative residuals.
empirical_evidence: Ground run mean EHI rises from 74.2 at t<15s to 94.6 at t>=60s. Excluding warm-up (t>=25s), fleet healthy mean reaches 95.82, fully satisfying H1.
mitigation_recommendation: Incorporate first-order thermal lag filter in surrogate reference or apply warm-up transient conditioning (grace period/transient tolerance window).

failure_name: Healthy EHI 5th Percentile Below Target (60.68 vs >=90.0)
affected_subsets: Ground Run scenarios (P5=59.38); specifically scenarios with large initial thermal deficits
key_timestamps: t in [0, 15] s in Ground Run flights
primary_root_cause: Exponential health mapping h_i = exp(-0.5*(d_i/beta)^2) penalizes large uncompensated thermal transients (|z| > 5 sigma) severely, pushing h_i down to 0.1-0.2.
empirical_evidence: At t in [0, 15]s in Ground Run, mean CHT residual is -38C (z = -6.2), EGT residual is -95C (z = -5.8). At t>=25s, healthy 5th percentile increases to 87.4, and at t>=35s to 92.1.
mitigation_recommendation: Adopt dynamic thermal reference modeling, transient tolerance expansion during engine warm-up, and bounded score rate-limiting.

failure_name: Physical Fault Severity Inversion on Unseen Engines (Mild=98.39, Mod=94.82, Sev=97.39)
affected_subsets: All physical fault classes across unseen engines; severe faults appear healthier than moderate faults
key_timestamps: All active post-onset timestamps across test engines
primary_root_cause: Unmodeled engine-to-engine baseline offsets (displacement V_d in [0.0006, 0.0012] m3, thermal efficiency in [0.22, 0.28]) confounded with unbalanced test scenario allocation. Engines with naturally lower baseline torque/power received moderate faults, while engines with higher baseline received severe faults.
empirical_evidence: Between-engine differences account for >90% of torque variance on normal flights. Within individual engines, severity ordering holds monotonically, but cross-engine aggregation causes Simpson's Paradox inversion.
mitigation_recommendation: Introduce online engine baseline adaptation (operating offset normalization) or relative delta-from-flight-baseline scoring instead of uncalibrated absolute population reference.

failure_name: Composite SDQI Insensitivity to Single-Sensor Faults (Measured ~94 vs <=75.0)
affected_subsets: All sensor fault classes (bias, drift, stuck, dropout)
primary_root_cause: Mathematical dilution of composite score: 10 channels with ~0.10 weight each mean that a total failure of ONE sensor (q_target=0) only reduces composite SDQI from 100 to 90. Furthermore, in-range bias (e.g. 35 RPM) rarely exceeds the 4-sigma analytical redundancy threshold.
empirical_evidence: Channel-level quality min(q_i) drops to 0.0 on stuck sensors (100% detection) and dropout (intermittent 0), yet composite SDQI averages 87.9 to 95.8 because 9 healthy channels (weight 0.90) remain at 100.
mitigation_recommendation: Redefine sensor data health: report worst-channel quality min_i(q_i) alongside composite SDQI, use non-linear penalty for degraded channels, and tune analytical redundancy thresholds to detect moderate in-range biases.

failure_name: Negative Correlation Between Throttle and EHI on Healthy Flights (r = -0.5918 / -0.4890)
affected_subsets: Healthy flights across all phases, especially Ground Run and Cruise
primary_root_cause: Heteroscedastic residual variance: at high throttle (80-95%), absolute sensor fluctuations and static reference errors scale proportionally with operating intensity, causing residuals to expand into the tolerance deadband (|z| > 2 sigma) and mildly depressing EHI from 100 to ~96.
empirical_evidence: Residual standard deviations at 90% throttle are 1.8x to 2.4x larger than at 30% throttle across CHT, EGT, vibration, and torque. Spearman rho is also negative (-0.52). Within cruise, r = -0.41.
mitigation_recommendation: Implement throttle-dependent adaptive residual normalization (heteroscedastic tolerance sigma(throttle)) or percentage-relative residual scaling.
